title: Tool permission engine: policies, allow, deny, always-rules
goal: The permission engine: decides allow / deny / ask for every tool use from policies and persisted always-rules, brokers approvals (local and delegated), and mirrors the CT-RBAC approver rules for the UI. Default is deny/ask, never silent allow.
scope_in: Rule model `{ id, tool: string, matcher?: { command?: string; path_glob?: string; mcp_server?: string }, action: 'allow'|'deny'|'ask', scope: 'session'|'project'|'user', created_at }` with evaluation order: explicit deny > explicit ask > explicit allow > mode default; first matching rule within a precedence class wins by most-specific matcher.

Permission modes mirroring the SDK: `default` (ask for writes/commands, allow reads in-scope), `acceptEdits` (allow edits inside the worktree, ask for commands), `plan` (deny all mutating tools), `bypassPermissions` (allow all except hard denies; requires explicit config opt-in and a visible warning flag `bypass_active`).

Hard denies that no rule or mode can override: writes outside the agent's root (worktree/cwd) after `realpath` resolution (symlink and `..` safe), writes to `.git/` internals, reads of known credential locations (`~/.ssh`, `~/.aws`, `~/.config/centcom/*token*`, OS keychain files), and any tool use while the agent is `stopped`.

Persistence: session rules in memory; project rules in `.centcom/permissions.local.json` (never committed: added to `.git/info/exclude`); user rules in `<config dir>/permissions.json`; atomic writes 0600; rule file schema validated, malformed file ignored with a warning (fail closed = no allow rules).
Always-rules from approvals: an approval with `scope: 'always'` creates a rule from the tool name plus a conservative matcher (exact command prefix up to the first flag/pipe; never `*` for Bash).

Approval broker: `requestApproval` creates a client-generated `apr_` id, `risk` (from `RiskClassifier`, default `medium` until lane C016 plugs in), `approver` (`host`|`owner`|`any_editor` per session policy), `expires_at` (default now + `agent.approval_timeout_ms`); resolves when a decision arrives with `decision: 'approve'|'deny'` and `scope: 'once'|'session'|'always'`; expiry resolves as deny.

Remote decisions: `resolveApproval(aprId, decision, from)` accepts a decision only when `from` is the host or satisfies the approver policy (CT-RBAC: host and delegated approvers); decisions from viewers/unknown members are ignored and surfaced to the audit callback.
Implements `PermissionGate` (from C013) so the runner can plug it in.
scope_out: Command parsing and risk scoring: lane C016 (this lane defines the `RiskClassifier` interface and a conservative default).
Rendering approval prompts: TUI/web lanes. Sending `approval.request`/`approval.decision` frames: session lanes.
Server-side enforcement of who may approve: the real relay; this lane only mirrors for UI and for the host's own safety checks.
Hooks (C022) and MCP (C021) which call into the gate.
build_against: Pure logic over injected fs, clock and ID generator; approvals exercised with synthetic decisions. Frames shapes (`approval.request` clear part `{approval_id, agent_id, risk, expires_at, approver}`; `approval.decision` `{approval_id, decision, scope}`) are validated with the generated validators; the mock backend (lane C007) is only needed in session-level tests elsewhere.
interfaces: `createPermissionEngine(deps: { fs: PermFs; clock: Clock; ids: IdGenerator; classifier?: RiskClassifier; config: PermConfig; audit: (e: AuditNote) => void; bus: AgentBus }): PermissionEngine`

`interface PermissionEngine extends PermissionGate { decide(req: ToolUseRequest, ctx: { agentId: AgentId; root: string; mode: PermissionMode }): Decision; requestApproval(req: ToolUseRequest, ctx): Promise<ApprovalOutcome>; resolveApproval(id: ApprovalId, d: { decision: 'approve'|'deny'; scope: 'once'|'session'|'always' }, from: { member: MemberId; role: 'host'|'editor'|'viewer'; delegated?: boolean }): ResolveResult; pending(): PendingApproval[]; addRule(r: NewRule): Promise<Rule>; removeRule(id: string): Promise<void>; listRules(): Rule[] }`

`type Decision = { behavior: 'allow'|'deny'|'ask'; reason: string; ruleId?: string; risk: 'low'|'medium'|'high' }`; `interface RiskClassifier { classify(req: ToolUseRequest): 'low'|'medium'|'high' }` (implemented by C016).
acceptance: Deny beats allow: with rules `allow Bash(git *)` and `deny Bash(git push*)`, `git push origin x` is denied and `git status` allowed.
`default` mode: Read of a file inside root -> allow; Edit -> ask; Bash `ls` -> ask unless a rule allows; `plan` mode: Edit and Bash -> deny with reason `plan_mode`.

A write to `<root>/../secrets.txt` and to a symlink inside root that points outside root are hard-denied in every mode including `bypassPermissions` (path traversal tests, POSIX and Windows case variants).
Approval with no response is denied at exactly `expires_at` (fake clock) and `pending()` is empty afterwards.

`resolveApproval` from a viewer or an unknown member returns `{accepted:false, reason:'not_approver'}` and calls `audit`; from the host or a delegated approver returns accepted:true and unblocks the waiting tool call within one tick.
An approval with `scope:'always'` for `Bash git status` creates a user/project rule that auto-allows `git status` next time but still asks for `git status; rm -rf x`.
A corrupted permissions.json yields zero allow rules, a warning, and the engine keeps asking; rule files are written 0600.
Approval payload produced for the wire passes the generated `approval.request` clear-schema validator and contains no command text or paths in the clear part.
tests: hard-deny.test.ts (traversal, symlink, Windows paths), broker.test.ts (expiry, delegation, duplicates).
wire-shape.test.ts, fuzz test on matcher parsing.
guardrails: MUST fail closed: any parsing error, missing rule file, unknown tool or classifier failure results in `ask` (or `deny` for hard-deny categories), never `allow`.
MUST resolve real paths (`realpath`, case-folded on case-insensitive FS) before comparing to the agent root; MUST NOT trust string prefixes.
MUST NOT allow `bypassPermissions` unless config explicitly enables it, and MUST still apply hard denies.
Client UIs mirror CT-RBAC for display only; this engine MUST NOT claim to be the authority for remote members -- the server enforces; the engine only decides what the local host does with a decision.
Approval ids MUST be fresh ULIDs from the CT-IDS generator; an `apr_` id can be resolved once (replay returns `already_resolved`).
The cleartext part of an approval MUST NOT contain the command, cwd, paths or summaries (those go in `ct`).
failure_modes: Approver never answers -> deny at expiry; agent receives a tool-denied message.
Two decisions race -> first accepted wins, second returns `already_resolved`.
Rule file locked/unwritable -> rule kept for the session only, user warned once.
notes: Delegated approvers are defined by CT-RBAC ('host (and delegated approvers)') but the wire has only `approver: host|owner|any_editor`; how delegation is granted is not specified. CONTRACT GAP: delegation mechanism (who is a delegated approver, how the client learns it). Implemented conservatively as: host always; `any_editor` honoured only if the session policy says so. SPLIT? engine vs approval broker could be separate PRs.
